title: Desmodromic valve gear is two rockers and two shims per valve — spring-valve assumptions do not transfer
description: A desmodromic engine closes its valves mechanically instead of with springs. Each valve has an opening rocker and a closing rocker, and two shims: a small one on top of the valve stem that sets the opening clearance, and a large one wrapped around the stem, retaining the collets, that sets the closing clearance. There is no bucket and no valve spring to compress. A mechanic who is fluent in shim-under-bucket work can still get this wrong, because the closing clearance has no equivalent in the engine they know and half the measurements they need do not exist on a spring-valve head. Written from general knowledge — every clearance figure, shim size and torque must come from the manual for the specific engine.
model: Desmodue, Desmoquattro, Testastretta, Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale engines
symptoms: no valve springs on this engine
shim under bucket method does not fit
causes: Desmodromic system closing valves with a second rocker rather than a spring, so there are two clearances per valve rather than one
Opening shim sitting on the valve stem and closing shim wrapping the stem to retain the collets — neither is a bucket shim
Mechanic applying shim-under-bucket experience where half the measurements have no equivalent
Workshop information for spring-valve engines being used on a desmodromic head
fix_procedure: 1. Confirm the engine is desmodromic before starting. Ducati road engines from the Desmodue through the Desmosedici Stradale are; the Multistrada V4's Granturismo is not, and uses conventional spring valve return. 2. Obtain the manual for the exact engine — clearance figures differ between 2-valve and 4-valve heads and between generations, and there is no safe generic figure. 3. SAFETY: cold engine only. Clearances are specified cold and a warm engine gives a false reading. 4. Understand what you are measuring before removing anything: per valve there is an opening clearance between the opening rocker and its shim, and a closing clearance at the closing rocker and its shim. Both are checked. 5. Set the engine to the position the manual specifies for the cylinder being measured, and do not turn the engine with belts or timing drive disturbed. 6. Record every measured clearance per valve before ordering shims — you are solving for two values per valve, not one. 7. Do not attempt to substitute spring-valve shims or procedures. The parts are not interchangeable and the method does not transfer.
parts_needed: Opening and closing shims in the sizes the measurements call for
Engine oil and filter if the service coincides with an oil change

title: Both desmo clearances must be measured — the closing clearance is the one with no spring-valve analogue
description: A spring-valve service produces one number per valve. A desmodromic service produces two, and the second — the closing clearance at the closing rocker — is the one a mechanic new to the system tends to skip or mis-measure, because nothing in a shim-under-bucket engine corresponds to it. Measuring only the opening side gives a service that looks complete, passes a road test, and has not actually been done. The two clearances also do not necessarily move in the same direction as an engine accumulates miles, so one being in specification says nothing about the other. Written from general knowledge — the clearance limits, the measuring method and the engine position for each cylinder must come from the manual.
model: Desmodue, Desmoquattro, Testastretta, Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale engines
symptoms: valve gear noisy after a service
causes: Closing clearance having no equivalent in a spring-valve engine, so it is skipped by a mechanic working from that background
A service sheet or invoice recording one clearance per valve rather than two
Closing clearance measured by an unfamiliar method and recorded incorrectly
Assuming a correct opening clearance implies a correct closing clearance
fix_procedure: 1. SAFETY: cold engine, correct engine position per the manual for each cylinder, and never rotate the engine with the timing drive disturbed. 2. Measure and record BOTH clearances for every valve — opening and closing — before ordering any shim. A record with one figure per valve is an incomplete service. 3. Use the manual's method for the closing clearance specifically; it is measured differently from the opening clearance and more than one technique exists. Where the manual describes a cross-check, do it. 4. Compare each measurement against the manual's limits for that engine, not against a remembered figure or another Ducati. 5. If a previous service recorded only opening clearances, treat the closing side as unmeasured regardless of what the invoice says. 6. Re-measure after fitting new shims and before reassembly — the point of the job is the final number, not the ordered part. 7. Record both figures per valve in the service history so the next service starts from real data.
parts_needed: Opening and closing shims as measured
Feeler gauges suitable for the manual's method

title: Closing shim collets and half-rings — the step where a desmo service goes badly wrong
description: The closing shim on a desmodromic valve wraps the valve stem and is retained by collets, sometimes called half-rings. Getting them seated correctly is the highest-consequence step in the whole service: a collet that is not fully home can release, and a valve that drops in a running engine destroys far more than the valve. There is a manufacturer tool for the job and shops do improvise, but improvising raises the stakes on the one step that must not be got wrong. This is the part of a desmo service that justifies the labour figure, and it is the reason a cheap desmo quote should be treated with suspicion. Written from general knowledge — follow the manual's procedure and use the specified tool.
model: Desmodue, Desmoquattro, Testastretta, Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale engines
symptoms: half rings loose on the stem
closing shim will not sit flat
causes: Collets not fully seated when the closing shim is refitted, allowing the retention to release in service
Improvised tooling used in place of the specified collet tool on a step with no margin for error
Reused collets or shims that are damaged, worn or mismatched
Time pressure on a labour-heavy job encouraging a rushed reassembly at exactly the wrong step
fix_procedure: 1. SAFETY: this step decides whether the engine survives. Do not rush it and do not improvise if you are unsure — a dropped valve in a running engine is a destroyed cylinder head at best. 2. Work clean. Any debris under a collet or shim prevents correct seating. 3. Inspect every collet and shim before refitting; replace anything worn, damaged or mismatched rather than reusing it. 4. Fit the closing shim and collets exactly per the manual, using the specified tool. Where a shop tool substitutes, confirm it holds the parts in the same relationship the factory tool does. 5. Verify seating positively before moving on — visually and by the manual's check, not by feel alone. 6. Re-measure the closing clearance after the collets are seated; a shim that is not sitting flat reads wrong and is the warning you get. 7. Turn the engine by hand through several full cycles before starting it, per the manual, and stop immediately if anything binds. 8. When quoting, price this step honestly. A desmo service is labour, and a quote that undercuts the labour is undercutting the care this step needs.
parts_needed: Closing shims in the measured sizes

title: Shim availability, not shim price, is what strands a Ducati mid-service
description: A desmo service produces two shim measurements per valve, and the sizes needed are not known until the engine is open and measured. Opening and closing shims come in many sizes, a shop cannot hold a full range of both, and the bike sits in pieces while parts are ordered. The customer experience of a desmo service is therefore dominated by lead time rather than by parts cost, and a shop that has not warned them will take the blame for a delay that was structural. Booking the job without planning for this is the most common scheduling mistake on these engines. Written from general knowledge — confirm shim ranges and availability for the specific engine with the supplier before booking.
model: Desmodue, Desmoquattro, Testastretta, Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale engines
symptoms: customer not warned about lead time
causes: Required shim sizes being unknowable until the engine is open and every valve measured
Two shim types per valve in many sizes, so no realistic shop stock covers the range
Supplier lead time on less common sizes, particularly closing shims for older engines
Job booked as a fixed-duration slot rather than one with a parts-ordering pause built in
fix_procedure: 1. When booking, tell the customer the bike will be stripped, measured, and then may wait for shims. Set that expectation before the bike arrives, not after. 2. Establish supplier availability and lead time for both shim types for this engine before the bike comes in. 3. Measure every valve and produce the complete shim list in one pass, so one order covers the job — a second order doubles the delay. 4. Order against measured figures only. Guessing sizes to save a day produces a second wrong order and a longer delay. 5. Protect the open engine while it waits: cover the head, keep parts organised and labelled by cylinder and valve, and keep debris out. 6. Where a size is unobtainable, ask the supplier about the nearest available and re-measure against the manual's tolerance rather than accepting a substitution blind. 7. Re-check clearances after fitting, before reassembly.
parts_needed: Opening and closing shims to the measured sizes
Covers or protection for an open engine awaiting parts

title: Desmo service intervals vary by generation — a remembered figure produces a wrong quote
description: Ducati desmo intervals are not one number. They differ substantially between the older air-cooled 2-valve engines, the liquid-cooled 4-valve engines, and the modern Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale, and they have generally lengthened over the years. A shop quoting from memory or from experience with a different Ducati will over-quote a modern bike or, worse, under-service an older one that needs attention far sooner than the figure they remember. The interval also drives the customer conversation more than any other number in this service, so getting it from the manual rather than from habit is the whole job. Written from general knowledge — take the interval for the exact model and year from the manual or from Ducati's schedule, never from another Ducati.
model: Desmodue, Desmoquattro, Testastretta, Superquadro and Desmosedici Stradale engines
symptoms: service schedule does not match bike
quote too high for a modern bike
unsure when desmo service is due
causes: Desmo intervals differing between 2-valve, 4-valve and modern engine families and lengthening over the model years
Shop applying an interval remembered from a different Ducati generation
Owner relying on general Ducati reputation rather than the schedule for their bike
Ducati's cam-belt and annual-service time limits being carried across to the valve clearances by analogy
fix_procedure: 1. Identify the exact model, year and engine before saying anything about interval or price. 2. Read the interval from the manual or Ducati's published schedule for that machine. Do not quote from another Ducati, however similar it looks. 3. Do not schedule the desmo service by age. On the manufacturer schedules read for this project the valve row is marked under distance columns only — the annual service is a separate row, and on the belt-driven engines it is the cam belts, not the clearances, that carry a months figure. Read the sheet for the model year in hand from the manual rather than assuming either rule. 4. Check the service history for what was actually done, not what was invoiced; a previous service that recorded only one clearance per valve was incomplete. 5. Quote the labour honestly against the manual's figure for that engine — access differs enormously between a 2-valve air-cooled twin and a modern 4-valve engine in a tight chassis. 6. Where a belt-driven engine is also due for belts, say so up front: the two jobs share access and doing them together saves the customer money, while discovering it mid-service does not. 7. Record model, engine and the schedule used in the job notes so the next quote starts correct.
parts_needed: Service items per the manual's schedule for the specific engine
Shims as measured once the engine is open

title: Two-valve and four-valve desmo services are different jobs — access and effort do not scale by cylinder count
description: An air-cooled 2-valve Desmodue and a liquid-cooled 4-valve Testastretta or Superquadro both need a desmo service, but the work is not comparable. The 2-valve engine has fewer valves and generally better access; the 4-valve engines have twice the valves, twice the shims again, and sit in tighter chassis with cooling and bodywork in the way. Estimating a 4-valve job from 2-valve experience — or the reverse — produces a quote that is wrong by a wide margin in one direction or the other, and it is a common source of jobs that overrun their booked slot. Written from general knowledge — take the labour figure for the specific engine from the manual.
model: Desmodue 2-valve versus Desmoquattro / Testastretta / Superquadro 4-valve engines
symptoms: quote based on a different ducati
twice as many shims as planned
causes: Four-valve heads carrying twice the valves and twice the shim measurements of a 2-valve head
Liquid-cooled engines in tight chassis needing bodywork, cooling and ancillaries removed for access
Labour estimated from experience with a different Ducati engine family
Cam belt work on belt-driven engines sharing access and being discovered mid-job rather than planned
fix_procedure: 1. Identify the engine family and count the valves before estimating. A 4-valve head is not a 2-valve job with more parts; it is roughly twice the measurement work plus the access. 2. Read the manual's disassembly sequence for the specific engine and estimate from that, not from the last Ducati that came through. 3. On liquid-cooled bikes, include bodywork, cooling and ancillary removal in the estimate — that access is often a significant share of the labour. 4. On belt-driven engines, check whether belts are also due and plan them into the same job, since the access overlaps. Belt procedure itself is a separate subject. 5. Build the shim-ordering pause into the booking rather than the slot. 6. SAFETY: cold engine throughout; on liquid-cooled engines do not open the cooling system warm. 7. Record actual hours against the engine family so the shop's next estimate improves.
parts_needed: Opening and closing shims as measured
Valve cover and access gaskets for the specific engine
Coolant if the cooling system is opened for access
